q1.sampleAnswer: Euler: y[n+1] = (1 + a Ts) y[n] + Ts u[n]; stability requires |1 + a Ts| < 1 (1 point). a > 0: always unstable, since Ts > 0 gives 1 + a Ts > 1 (1 point). a = 0: stable for all Ts (1 point). a < 0: stable if Ts < 2/|a| (1 point).

q2.sampleAnswer: Build M = [[a, 1], [0, 0]]. Correspondence requires I + Ts A = sum_k (M Ts)^k / k! (1 point), i.e. M^2 = [[a^2, a], [0, 0]] = 0 (1 point), which holds only for a = 0 (1 point).

q3.sampleAnswer: Non-linear (affine) for all a (1 point); time-invariant for all a, since cos(2 pi n) = 1 is constant (1 point; a convincing argument for time-variance also gets full marks); memoryless only for a = 0 (1 point); causal and stable for |a| < 1, anti-causal and stable for |a| > 1 (3 points; only 1.5 if the anti-causal case is missing). In general 0.5 points each for a correct conclusion and a correct argument.

q4.sampleAnswer: u[n] * h_2[n] = a^n s[n] - a^n s[n-1] = delta[n]: the output is a unit impulse.

q5.sampleAnswer: LTI systems commute, so u * (h_2 * h_1) = (u * h_2) * h_1 (3 points). The output is therefore the impulse response of G_1: delta[n] * sin(8n) = sin(8n) (2 points). Small errors: -0.5 or -1 point.

q6.sampleAnswer: sum 1/n^2 converges, so x is absolutely summable and X(Omega) exists (1 point). By linearity q = x + F^-1(e^(j Omega) X) (1 point), and F^-1(e^(j Omega) X) = {x[n+1]}, so q[n] = x[n] + x[n+1] (2 points). q = {..., 0 (n=0), 1/2^2, 1/2^2, 1/4^2, 1/4^2, ...} (1 point). Hence r[2] = 1/2^2 - 0, r[4] = 1/4^2 - 1/2^2, and in general r[n] = 1/n^2 - 1/(n-2)^2 for even n >= 4, with r[n] = 0 for n <= 0 and odd n (1 point; -0.5 if n = 2 is missing).

q7.sampleAnswer: z[n+N] = sum_k x[k] / y[n+N-k] = sum_k x[k] / y[n-k] = z[n], so z is periodic (1 point) with period N (1 point).

q8.sampleAnswer: Z[k] = 1/N sum_n sum_r x[r]/y[n-r] e^(-j2k pi/N n); splitting the exponential as e^(-j2k pi/N (n-r)) e^(-j2k pi/N r) and reordering the sums gives Z[k] = N X[k] W[k] (1 point per step). Marked rigorously: the steps must be shown; the bare result X[k] W[k] gets 0 points.

q9.sampleAnswer: Write u with frequencies Omega_0 = 0, Omega_1 = pi, Omega_2 = pi/3 (1 point). Need H(1) = 1, H(-1) = 0, H(e^(+-j pi/3)) = 0 (1 point each). FIR guarantees stability (1 point); causality by multiplying by z^-N (1 point). H(z) = alpha (z + 1)(z^2 - z + 1) z^-3 = alpha (1 + z^-3) (1 point); H(1) = 1 gives alpha = 1/2 (1 point), so H(z) = (1 + z^-3)/2 and y[n] = (u[n] + u[n-3])/2 (1 point). An order-6 moving average is also accepted.

q12.sampleAnswer: An LTI relationship exists; it only requires H(e^(j)) = 2 (H at Omega = 1), so the system is not unique.

q13.sampleAnswer: An LTI relationship exists and is uniquely defined: H(Omega) = 2 (i.e. y = 2u).

q14.sampleAnswer: An LTI relationship exists because both signals are periodic with the same fundamental period, but it is not unique: only the values H(e^(j 2pi k/12)) are specified, the rest of H(Omega) is arbitrary.
